**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 72, verses 1–15:**

Makkiyya. It has eight hundred and seventy-two letters, eighty-five words, and twenty-eight verses.

Nafil ibn Raqim ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Babi informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi related to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad al-Karbasi related to us, saying: Asbat ibn al-Yasa' al-Bukhari related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abdullah al-Sulami related to us, saying: Nuh ibn Abi Maryam related to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Jinn will be given, for every jinn and devil who believed in Muhammad and denied him, the reward of freeing a slave." [38] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/140.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened, and they said: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord."﴾ They were nine jinn from the jinn of Nasibin who listened to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ), and their story has already passed. [[See Musnad Ahmad: 1/458.]]

Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: We have been told that they were from the children of Satan, and they are the most numerous of the jinn and the general soldiers of Iblis.

﴿So they said, when they returned to their people: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an"...﴾ and "annahu" with a fatha was read by the people of Syria and Kufa except Hafs.

Abu Ja'far read with a fatha what was connected to the revelation (waḥy), and with a kasra what was a report about the jinn, and the rest read all of it with a kasra.

﴿Exalted is the majesty (jadd) of our Lord.﴾ Abu ... [translated as it stands]

Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Adl related to us, saying: al-Asamm related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying "jadd rabbina," who said: "The command of our Lord."

And with his chain from Sufyan, from Salman al-Taymi, from al-Hasan, who said: "The wealth of our Lord"; from this it is said that luck is "jadd," and a fortunate man is "majdud." Ibn Abbas said: "The power of our Lord." Mujahid and Ikrimah: "His majesty." Qatada: "His greatness." Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid: "His remembrance." Dahhak: "His action." al-Qurazi: "His blessings and favours upon His creation." al-Akhfash: "The kingship of our Lord has exalted." Ibn Kaysan: "His victory over every disbeliever by argument." And "al-jadd" in the language means greatness, and from it is the saying of Anas:

"When a man recited al-Baqara and Al 'Imran, he became great (jadd) in our eyes," i.e., great.

Ibn Abbas said: "Had I known that there was any fortune (jadd) among mankind, they would not have said 'Exalted is the jadd of our Lord.'"

Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, his son Ja'far, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "God has no jadd; rather, the jadd belongs to the ignorant, so you were not held accountable for it."

﴿He has not taken a consort nor a son.﴾ Ikrimah read "Taala jiddu rabbina" with a kasra on the jim, in opposition to jest (hazl). Ibn al-Sumay' read "jiddi rabbina," meaning benefit and profit.

﴿And that the foolish one among us (safihuna) used to say about Allah an outrageous lie (shatat)﴾: "safihuna" means our ignorant one. Mujahid and Qatada said: It is Iblis, may Allah curse him. "Shatat" means transgression and grave utterance.

﴿And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never speak a lie against Allah﴾, i.e., we used to think they were truthful in their saying that Allah has a consort and a son, until we heard the Qur'an.

﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq﴾: This is the saying of an Arab man when he reaches a desolate land at nightfall: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the evil of the foolish ones of his people," and he spends the night in security and protection until morning.

Muqatil said: The first to seek refuge with the jinn were a people from Yemen, then the Banu Hanifa, then this spread among the Arabs.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Abu al-Qayyim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Marwazi related to us, saying: Musa ibn Sa'id ibn al-Nu'man related to us in Tartus, saying: Farwa ibn Mu'raa al-Kindi related to us, saying: al-Qayyim ibn Malik related to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from his father, from Kurdam ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Ansari, who said: I went out with my father to Medina on a need, and that was the first time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned in Mecca. Night fell on us at the house of a shepherd. When midday came, a wolf came and seized a lamb from the flock, so the shepherd leapt up and said: "O protector of the valley, your protection!" Then a voice we could not see called out: "O Sirhan, release it!" The lamb came running until it entered the flock, and it was not even bruised. He said: And Allah the Exalted revealed to His Messenger in Mecca: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq﴾.

That is: [the humans increased the jinn in transgression by their seeking refuge] so they increased them in rahaq.

Ibn Abbas said: "Sin (athm)." Ma'mar from Qatada: "Error (khati'a)." Sa'id from him: "Audacity (jur'a)." [In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Disbelief (kufr)."] Mujahid: "Transgression (tughyan)."

Rabi': "Fear (faraq)." Ibn Zayd: "Dread (khawf)." Ibrahim: "Greatness (azama), for they said: 'We have become lords (sadana) over the jinn and mankind.'" Muqatil: "Error (ghayya)." al-Hasan: "Evil (sharr)." Tha'lab: "Loss (khasar)." And "rahaq" in the speech of the Arabs means sin and the committing of what is forbidden, and a man who does so is "murhiq." al-A'sha said:

"Nothing benefits me apart from seeing her... Does the lover find healing unless he has been touched by rahaq?"

﴿And that they thought, as you thought, O disbelievers among mankind, that Allah would never resurrect anyone after his death.﴾ ﴿And that we touched the heaven and found it filled with a strong guard (harasan shadidan) of angels and with meteors (shuhuban) from the stars.﴾ ﴿And that we used to sit in it from the heaven in seats for listening; so whoever listens now will find for himself a watching meteor (shihaban rasadan).﴾ ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth by the hurling of meteors, or whether their Lord intends for them guidance (rashadan).﴾ ﴿And that among us are the righteous, and among us are others beneath that; we were divided into diverse sects (tara'iq qidadan), differing desires and various groups: among us is the believer and among us is the disbeliever.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Diverse colours (alwanan shatta)." al-Hasan: "Differing sorts (qiddan mukhtalifin)." al-Akhfash: "Kinds (darban)." Abu Ubayda: "Categories (asnafan)." al-Mu'arrikh: "Races (ajnasan)." al-Nadr: "Religions (milal)." Ibn Kaysan: "Factions and groups, each with a desire like the desires of people." al-Farra' said: The Arabs say: "These are the path (tariqa) of their people," meaning their chiefs and leaders. al-Musayyab: "We were Muslims, Jews, and Christians."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Khattab related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Nahtawayh related to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Suri at Antioch related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil ibn Abi al-Sarri related to us, saying: al-Muttalib ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi say regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted, "kunna tara'iqa qidadan": "The jinn are like you; among them are Qadariyya, Murji'a, Rafida, and Shi'a."

The singular of "qidad" is "qidda," which is a sect, and its origin is from "qadd," which is cutting. Labid lamented his brother Arbad:

"The eye did not reach all its fill on a night when the horses walked like cut sections (qidad)."

And another said:

"I said, and Zayd the bold was with me, on the day when the horses of Amr turned in sections (qidadan)."

﴿And that we thought we would never be able to escape Allah in the earth if He intended some matter for us, nor could we flee from Him by running away.﴾ ﴿And that when we heard the guidance, we believed in it; so whoever believes in his Lord will not fear diminution (bakhsan) nor injustice (rahaqan).﴾ The common readers recite it with an alif; al-A'mash read "fala yakhaf" with the jussive. "Bakhsan": loss. "Rahaqan": oppression. He says: he does not fear that his good deeds will be diminished, nor that his evil deeds will be increased, nor that he will be taken to account for another's sin, nor that he will be punished without guilt. It was also said: "rahaqan" means something hateful that overtakes him; and it was said: it means the total loss of it. Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He will not fear injustice nor diminution﴾ [[Surat Taha: 112.]].

﴿And that among us are the Muslims, and among us are the unjust (al-qasitun), those who deviate from the truth.﴾ It is said: "aqsata al-rajul" means he is "muqsit" if he was just. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And act justly; indeed, Allah loves the just﴾ [[Surat al-Hujurat: 9.]]. And "qasata yaqsutu qusuran" means he was unjust. The poet said:

"A people who killed the son of Hind by force, Amr, and they were unjust toward al-Nu'man."

And Ibn Zayd recited:

"We were unjust toward the kings in the era of Tubba', and before that I do not know the consequences for souls."

Its counterpart in speech is "al-mutarrib" (the poor) and "al-mutrib" (the rich).

﴿So whoever submits, those have sought out right guidance (rashadan)﴾, i.e., they aimed, prepared, and intended; and from it is "taharrī al-qibla" for one whose direction is obscured. Imru' al-Qays said:

"A heavy rain in which there is abundance, covering the earth, seeking out and watering."

﴿As for the unjust, they will be fuel (hataban) for Hell.﴾

﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened, and they said: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord."﴾ They were nine jinn from the jinn of Nasibin who listened to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ), and their story has already passed. [[See Musnad Ahmad: 1/458.]]

Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: We have been told that they were from the children of Satan, and they are the most numerous of the jinn and the general soldiers of Iblis.

﴿So they said, when they returned to their people: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an"...﴾ and "annahu" with a fatha was read by the people of Syria and Kufa except Hafs.

Abu Ja'far read with a fatha what was connected to the revelation (waḥy), and with a kasra what was a report about the jinn, and the rest read all of it with a kasra.

﴿Exalted is the majesty (jadd) of our Lord.﴾ Abu ... [translated as it stands]

Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Adl related to us, saying: al-Asamm related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying "jadd rabbina," who said: "The command of our Lord."

And with his chain from Sufyan, from Salman al-Taymi, from al-Hasan, who said: "The wealth of our Lord"; from this it is said that luck is "jadd," and a fortunate man is "majdud." Ibn Abbas said: "The power of our Lord." Mujahid and Ikrimah: "His majesty." Qatada: "His greatness." Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid: "His remembrance." Dahhak: "His action." al-Qurazi: "His blessings and favours upon His creation." al-Akhfash: "The kingship of our Lord has exalted." Ibn Kaysan: "His victory over every disbeliever by argument." And "al-jadd" in the language means greatness, and from it is the saying of Anas:

"When a man recited al-Baqara and Al 'Imran, he became great (jadd) in our eyes," i.e., great.

Ibn Abbas said: "Had I known that there was any fortune (jadd) among mankind, they would not have said 'Exalted is the jadd of our Lord.'"

Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, his son Ja'far, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "God has no jadd; rather, the jadd belongs to the ignorant, so you were not held accountable for it."

﴿He has not taken a consort nor a son.﴾ Ikrimah read "Taala jiddu rabbina" with a kasra on the jim, in opposition to jest (hazl). Ibn al-Sumay' read "jiddi rabbina," meaning benefit and profit.

﴿And that the foolish one among us (safihuna) used to say about Allah an outrageous lie (shatat)﴾: "safihuna" means our ignorant one. Mujahid and Qatada said: It is Iblis, may Allah curse him. "Shatat" means transgression and grave utterance.

﴿And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never speak a lie against Allah﴾, i.e., we used to think they were truthful in their saying that Allah has a consort and a son, until we heard the Qur'an.

﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq﴾: This is the saying of an Arab man when he reaches a desolate land at nightfall: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the evil of the foolish ones of his people," and he spends the night in security and protection until morning.

Muqatil said: The first to seek refuge with the jinn were a people from Yemen, then the Banu Hanifa, then this spread among the Arabs.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Abu al-Qayyim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Marwazi related to us, saying: Musa ibn Sa'id ibn al-Nu'man related to us in Tartus, saying: Farwa ibn Mu'raa al-Kindi related to us, saying: al-Qayyim ibn Malik related to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from his father, from Kurdam ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Ansari, who said: I went out with my father to Medina on a need, and that was the first time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned in Mecca. Night fell on us at the house of a shepherd. When midday came, a wolf came and seized a lamb from the flock, so the shepherd leapt up and said: "O protector of the valley, your protection!" Then a voice we could not see called out: "O Sirhan, release it!" The lamb came running until it entered the flock, and it was not even bruised. He said: And Allah the Exalted revealed to His Messenger in Mecca: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq﴾.

That is: [the humans increased the jinn in transgression by their seeking refuge] so they increased them in rahaq.

Ibn Abbas said: "Sin (athm)." Ma'mar from Qatada: "Error (khati'a)." Sa'id from him: "Audacity (jur'a)." [In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Disbelief (kufr)."] Mujahid: "Transgression (tughyan)."

Rabi': "Fear (faraq)." Ibn Zayd: "Dread (khawf)." Ibrahim: "Greatness (azama), for they said: 'We have become lords (sadana) over the jinn and mankind.'" Muqatil: "Error (ghayya)." al-Hasan: "Evil (sharr)." Tha'lab: "Loss (khasar)." And "rahaq" in the speech of the Arabs means sin and the committing of what is forbidden, and a man who does so is "murhiq." al-A'sha said:

"Nothing benefits me apart from seeing her... Does the lover find healing unless he has been touched by rahaq?"

﴿And that they thought, as you thought, O disbelievers among mankind, that Allah would never resurrect anyone after his death.﴾ ﴿And that we touched the heaven and found it filled with a strong guard (harasan shadidan) of angels and with meteors (shuhuban) from the stars.﴾ ﴿And that we used to sit in it from the heaven in seats for listening; so whoever listens now will find for himself a watching meteor (shihaban rasadan).﴾ ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth by the hurling of meteors, or whether their Lord intends for them guidance (rashadan).﴾ ﴿And that among us are the righteous, and among us are others beneath that; we were divided into diverse sects (tara'iq qidadan), differing desires and various groups: among us is the believer and among us is the disbeliever.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Diverse colours (alwanan shatta)." al-Hasan: "Differing sorts (qiddan mukhtalifin)." al-Akhfash: "Kinds (darban)." Abu Ubayda: "Categories (asnafan)." al-Mu'arrikh: "Races (ajnasan)." al-Nadr: "Religions (milal)." Ibn Kaysan: "Factions and groups, each with a desire like the desires of people." al-Farra' said: The Arabs say: "These are the path (tariqa) of their people," meaning their chiefs and leaders. al-Musayyab: "We were Muslims, Jews, and Christians."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Khattab related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Nahtawayh related to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Suri at Antioch related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil ibn Abi al-Sarri related to us, saying: al-Muttalib ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi say regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted, "kunna tara'iqa qidadan": "The jinn are like you; among them are Qadariyya, Murji'a, Rafida, and Shi'a."

The singular of "qidad" is "qidda," which is a sect, and its origin is from "qadd," which is cutting. Labid lamented his brother Arbad:

"The eye did not reach all its fill on a night when the horses walked like cut sections (qidad)."

And another said:

"I said, and Zayd the bold was with me, on the day when the horses of Amr turned in sections (qidadan)."

﴿And that we thought we would never be able to escape Allah in the earth if He intended some matter for us, nor could we flee from Him by running away.﴾ ﴿And that when we heard the guidance, we believed in it; so whoever believes in his Lord will not fear diminution (bakhsan) nor injustice (rahaqan).﴾ The common readers recite it with an alif; al-A'mash read "fala yakhaf" with the jussive. "Bakhsan": loss. "Rahaqan": oppression. He says: he does not fear that his good deeds will be diminished, nor that his evil deeds will be increased, nor that he will be taken to account for another's sin, nor that he will be punished without guilt. It was also said: "rahaqan" means something hateful that overtakes him; and it was said: it means the total loss of it. Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He will not fear injustice nor diminution﴾ [[Surat Taha: 112.]].

﴿And that among us are the Muslims, and among us are the unjust (al-qasitun), those who deviate from the truth.﴾ It is said: "aqsata al-rajul" means he is "muqsit" if he was just. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And act justly; indeed, Allah loves the just﴾ [[Surat al-Hujurat: 9.]]. And "qasata yaqsutu qusuran" means he was unjust. The poet said:

"A people who killed the son of Hind by force, Amr, and they were unjust toward al-Nu'man."

And Ibn Zayd recited:

"We were unjust toward the kings in the era of Tubba', and before that I do not know the consequences for souls."

Its counterpart in speech is "al-mutarrib" (the poor) and "al-mutrib" (the rich).

﴿So whoever submits, those have sought out right guidance (rashadan)﴾, i.e., they aimed, prepared, and intended; and from it is "taharrī al-qibla" for one whose direction is obscured. Imru' al-Qays said:

"A heavy rain in which there is abundance, covering the earth, seeking out and watering."

﴿As for the unjust, they will be fuel (hataban) for Hell.﴾

Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Adl related to us, saying: al-Asamm related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying "jadd rabbina," who said: "The command of our Lord."

[38] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/140.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

[[See Musnad Ahmad: 1/458.]]

Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: We have been told that they were from the children of Satan, and they are the most numerous of the jinn and the general soldiers of Iblis.

Abu Ja'far read with a fatha what was connected to the revelation (waḥy), and with a kasra what was a report about the jinn, and the rest read all of it with a kasra.

﴿Exalted is the majesty (jadd) of our Lord.﴾ Abu ... [translated as it stands]

Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Adl related to us, saying: al-Asamm related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying "jadd rabbina," who said: "The command of our Lord."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 72, verse 16–28:

﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا﴾ The reading of the common readers (al-'amma) is "law" with a kasra on the waw. Al-A'mash read "lawu" with a damma on the waw.

﴿عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ The exegetes differed in its interpretation. A group said: its meaning is, "And that if they had remained upon the way of truth, faith and guidance, and had been believers and obedient," ﴿لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ ماءً غَدَقاً﴾. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding this verse: "Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is trial (fitna)." He meant: We would have given them much wealth, a comfortable life, widened their provision and spread out for them in this world, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ that We might test them, to see how they would thank Him for what they were granted. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, Qatada, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Atiyya, Muqatil and al-Hasan. He said: "By Allah, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were listening to Allah and obeying Him when the treasures of Kisra and Caesar were opened to them, and they were tested by them, so they rose against their Imam and killed him, meaning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 66.] And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 96.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَياةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 97.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً﴾ [Surah Nuh: 10–11.] and other verses.

Others said: its meaning is, ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى طريقة الكفر والضلالة﴾ "And that if they had remained upon the way of disbelief and misguidance, and had all been disbelievers, We would have given them much wealth and widened for them, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ as a punishment for them and a gradual leading (istidraj), until they would be tested and We would punish them."

This is the view of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Kalbi, al-Thumali, Yaman ibn Rabab, Ibn Kaysan and Ibn Mujallad. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 44.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 33.]

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 27.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ [Surah al-'Alaq: 6–7.]

﴿وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ﴾ The readers of Kufa, Ya'qub and Ayyub read it with the letter ya (yaslukhu, "He will cause him to enter"), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd. Muslim ibn Jundab read "nuslikhu" with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the lam. The others read it with a fatha on the nun and a damma on the lam. Both are dialectal forms: "salaka" and "aslaka" have the same meaning, namely "to cause to enter."

﴿عَذاباً صَعَداً﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Arduous." Al-Suddi: "Hardship." Qatada: "There is no relief in it." Muqatil: "There is no release in it." Al-Hasan: "It only increases in severity."

Ibn Zayd: "Exhausting." The root meaning of this is that ascending (su'ud) is difficult for a person, and from it is 'Umar's saying: "Nothing has made me climb (tasa'uduni) as much as a marriage proposal," meaning it was difficult for me. 'Ikrima said: it is a mountain in the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira will be commanded to ascend in the Fire a mountain of smooth rock, until he reaches its summit, being pulled from in front with chains and struck with iron maces, until he reaches its top, yet he will not reach it for forty years. When he reaches its top, he will be dragged down to its base, and then he will again be commanded to ascend it. That is his condition forever. This is His saying: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾ [Surah al-Muddaththir: 17.]

﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The jinn said to the Prophet of Allah: "How can we come to the mosque and witness the prayer with you, when we are far from you?" So this was revealed: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾.

Qatada said: When the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated partners with Allah, so Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers to make their supplication purely for Him when they entered the mosques, and He meant by it all the mosques.

Al-Hasan said: He meant by it all the lands, because the earth was made a mosque for the Prophet (ﷺ), and after the revelation of this verse, when one of the Muslims entered a mosque he would say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Talq ibn Habib said: By "mosques" is meant the limbs upon which the servant prostrates, and they are seven: the two feet, the two knees, the two hands and the face. I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sulami say:

I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qayyim al-Bazzaz say: Ibn 'Ata' said: "Your mosques are your limbs upon which you were commanded to prostrate; do not abase them to other than their Creator."

And Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya informed us more than once, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Hamdan al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il, Mu'alla ibn Asad and Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, they said: Wuhayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Tawus narrated to us from his father from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to prostrate upon seven: the bridge of the nose (indicating his nose with his hand), the forehead, the two hands, the two knees and the tips of the two feet, and that I should not gather up hair or clothing." [39] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/292.]

And Abu Bakr al-Juzuqi informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Basri informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to us from Ibn al-Had from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from 'Amir ibn Sa'd from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the servant prostrates, seven prostrate with him." [40] [Kitab al-Musnad li al-Shafi'i: 40.]

If "mosques" is taken to mean places, its singular is "masjid" with a kasra on the jim; if it is taken to mean the limbs, its singular is "masjid" with a fatha on the jim.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾ means the prayers. ﴿فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾ means: single Him out with tawhid and devote worship to Him sincerely. It was said: its meaning is, devote them to the remembrance of Allah and His worship, so do not make them a marketplace, a meeting place or a thoroughfare, and do not allot to other than Allah any share in them.

﴿وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ﴾ meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿يَدْعُوهُ﴾ saying: "There is no god but Allah," and calling to Him and reciting the Qur'an, ﴿كادُوا﴾ meaning the jinn, ﴿يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً﴾ meaning they would ride upon one another, crowd and fall over one another, out of eagerness to listen to the Qur'an. This was said by al-Dahhak, and 'Ata' related it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from him: This is the words of a group of the jinn when they returned to their people and informed them of what they had seen of the obedience of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to him, and their concern for him in bowing and prostration, and their following him in prayer.

Al-Hasan, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: It means that when 'Abd Allah stood with the call, the jinn and the humans gathered together and backed one another against him, to nullify the truth he had brought and to extinguish the light of Allah. But Allah refused except to complete this matter, support it and make it prevail over those who opposed it.

The root of "lubad" is groups piled upon one another; from it the large locust is called "labad," and hair is said to be "tallabbada" when it accumulates. From it the mane (lubda) of a lion takes its name, and its plural is "lubad." Zuhayr said:

*Before a lion, armed with weapons, fierce, having a mane whose claws have not been trimmed.* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/24.]

It has four readings: "lubad" with a kasra on the lam and a fatha on the ba' — and this is the reading of the common readers and the choice of Abu 'Ubayda and Abu Hatim, its singular being "lubda" with a kasra on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba', which is the reading of Mujahid and Ibn Muhays, its singular being "lubda" with a damma on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on both the lam and the ba', which is the reading of Abu Haywa, its singular being "lubayd"; and "lubbad" with a damma on the lam and a shadda on the ba', which is the reading of al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far, its singular being "labid," like "raki'" (kneeling) from "raka'a" and "sajid" from "sajada."

﴿قالَ﴾ meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is with this reading that most of the readers recited. Abu Ja'far, al-A'mash, 'Asim and Hamza read ﴿قُلْ﴾ as an imperative: ﴿إِنَّما أَدْعُوا رَبِّي وَلا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ أَحَدٌ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً﴾ meaning a refuge to which I may incline. Qatada said: "Support." Al-Kalbi: "An entrance into the earth like a tunnel." Al-Suddi: "A refuge."

Muqatil said: The Quraysh disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You have come with a great matter the like of which has never been heard, and you have opposed all the people. So return from this matter, and we will reward you." So Allah revealed these verses.

In the reading of Ubayy: "'anna wa la rashadan" (instead of "lakum darran wa la rashadan").

﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِسالاتِهِ﴾ for in it is the return, the security and the deliverance, said al-Hasan.

Qatada said: ﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ — that is what I possess, by the help and success of Allah; as for disbelief and faith, I do not possess them.

It was said: ﴿لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً﴾ — but I convey a message from Allah; I am only a messenger and a conveyor, possessing nothing except what I have been given.

﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً﴾ ﴿حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا ما يُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment.

﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ ناصِراً وَأَقَلُّ عَدَداً﴾ ﴿قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment; it was also said: the Resurrection. ﴿أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أَمَداً﴾ a term whose duration is long, an extended end.

﴿عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ﴾ is in the nominative as an adjective of "my Lord" (rabbi). It was also said: it is "the Knower of the unseen." ﴿فَلا يُظْهِرُ﴾ He does not cause to know ﴿عَلى غَيْبِهِ أَحَداً﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضى﴾ chosen ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a messenger; for He chooses him and informs him of what He wills of the unseen.

﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ He mentions some directions as an indication of all of them, ﴿رَصَداً﴾ guardians from among the angels who protect him from the devils and from the jinn's eavesdropping, lest they steal something and convey it to their soothsayers.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: ﴿رَصَداً﴾ are four guardian angels. Muqatil and others said: When Allah sent a messenger, Iblis would come to him in the form of Jibril to inform him. So Allah sent, ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً﴾ angels to guard him and drive away the devil. When a devil came to him in the form of an angel, they would say: "This is a devil, so beware." And when an angel came to him, they would say: "This is the messenger of your Lord."

﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ya', meaning: that people may know that the messengers have conveyed. The others read it with a fatha on the ya', meaning: that the Messenger may know that the angels ﴿أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ have conveyed the messages of their Lord. ﴿وَأَحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ — with what is with them, ﴿وَأَحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَداً﴾ so that nothing was hidden from him. "'Adadan" is in the accusative as a circumstantial (ḥāl); and if you wish, as a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning he counted a counting.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 72, verse 16–28:

﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا﴾ The reading of the common readers (al-'amma) is "law" with a kasra on the waw. Al-A'mash read "lawu" with a damma on the waw.

﴿عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ The exegetes differed in its interpretation. A group said: its meaning is, "And that if they had remained upon the way of truth, faith and guidance, and had been believers and obedient," ﴿لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ ماءً غَدَقاً﴾. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding this verse: "Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is trial (fitna)." He meant: We would have given them much wealth, a comfortable life, widened their provision and spread out for them in this world, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ that We might test them, to see how they would thank Him for what they were granted. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, Qatada, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Atiyya, Muqatil and al-Hasan. He said: "By Allah, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were listening to Allah and obeying Him when the treasures of Kisra and Caesar were opened to them, and they were tested by them, so they rose against their Imam and killed him, meaning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 66.] And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 96.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَياةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 97.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً﴾ [Surah Nuh: 10–11.] and other verses.

Others said: its meaning is, ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى طريقة الكفر والضلالة﴾ "And that if they had remained upon the way of disbelief and misguidance, and had all been disbelievers, We would have given them much wealth and widened for them, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ as a punishment for them and a gradual leading (istidraj), until they would be tested and We would punish them."

This is the view of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Kalbi, al-Thumali, Yaman ibn Rabab, Ibn Kaysan and Ibn Mujallad. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 44.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 33.]

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 27.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ [Surah al-'Alaq: 6–7.]

﴿وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ﴾ The readers of Kufa, Ya'qub and Ayyub read it with the letter ya (yaslukhu, "He will cause him to enter"), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd. Muslim ibn Jundab read "nuslikhu" with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the lam. The others read it with a fatha on the nun and a damma on the lam. Both are dialectal forms: "salaka" and "aslaka" have the same meaning, namely "to cause to enter."

Ibn Zayd: "Exhausting." The root meaning of this is that ascending (su'ud) is difficult for a person, and from it is 'Umar's saying: "Nothing has made me climb (tasa'uduni) as much as a marriage proposal," meaning it was difficult for me. 'Ikrima said: it is a mountain in the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira will be commanded to ascend in the Fire a mountain of smooth rock, until he reaches its summit, being pulled from in front with chains and struck with iron maces, until he reaches its top, yet he will not reach it for forty years. When he reaches its top, he will be dragged down to its base, and then he will again be commanded to ascend it. That is his condition forever. This is His saying: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾ [Surah al-Muddaththir: 17.]

﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The jinn said to the Prophet of Allah: "How can we come to the mosque and witness the prayer with you, when we are far from you?" So this was revealed: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾.

Qatada said: When the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated partners with Allah, so Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers to make their supplication purely for Him when they entered the mosques, and He meant by it all the mosques.

Al-Hasan said: He meant by it all the lands, because the earth was made a mosque for the Prophet (ﷺ), and after the revelation of this verse, when one of the Muslims entered a mosque he would say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Talq ibn Habib said: By "mosques" is meant the limbs upon which the servant prostrates, and they are seven: the two feet, the two knees, the two hands and the face. I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sulami say:

I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qayyim al-Bazzaz say: Ibn 'Ata' said: "Your mosques are your limbs upon which you were commanded to prostrate; do not abase them to other than their Creator."

And Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya informed us more than once, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Hamdan al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il, Mu'alla ibn Asad and Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, they said: Wuhayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Tawus narrated to us from his father from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to prostrate upon seven: the bridge of the nose (indicating his nose with his hand), the forehead, the two hands, the two knees and the tips of the two feet, and that I should not gather up hair or clothing." [39] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/292.]

And Abu Bakr al-Juzuqi informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Basri informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to us from Ibn al-Had from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from 'Amir ibn Sa'd from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the servant prostrates, seven prostrate with him." [40] [Kitab al-Musnad li al-Shafi'i: 40.]

If "mosques" is taken to mean places, its singular is "masjid" with a kasra on the jim; if it is taken to mean the limbs, its singular is "masjid" with a fatha on the jim.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾ means the prayers. ﴿فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾ means: single Him out with tawhid and devote worship to Him sincerely. It was said: its meaning is, devote them to the remembrance of Allah and His worship, so do not make them a marketplace, a meeting place or a thoroughfare, and do not allot to other than Allah any share in them.

﴿وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ﴾ meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿يَدْعُوهُ﴾ saying: "There is no god but Allah," and calling to Him and reciting the Qur'an, ﴿كادُوا﴾ meaning the jinn, ﴿يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً﴾ meaning they would ride upon one another, crowd and fall over one another, out of eagerness to listen to the Qur'an. This was said by al-Dahhak, and 'Ata' related it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from him: This is the words of a group of the jinn when they returned to their people and informed them of what they had seen of the obedience of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to him, and their concern for him in bowing and prostration, and their following him in prayer.

Al-Hasan, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: It means that when 'Abd Allah stood with the call, the jinn and the humans gathered together and backed one another against him, to nullify the truth he had brought and to extinguish the light of Allah. But Allah refused except to complete this matter, support it and make it prevail over those who opposed it.

The root of "lubad" is groups piled upon one another; from it the large locust is called "labad," and hair is said to be "tallabbada" when it accumulates. From it the mane (lubda) of a lion takes its name, and its plural is "lubad." Zuhayr said:

*Before a lion, armed with weapons, fierce, having a mane whose claws have not been trimmed.* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/24.]

It has four readings: "lubad" with a kasra on the lam and a fatha on the ba' — and this is the reading of the common readers and the choice of Abu 'Ubayda and Abu Hatim, its singular being "lubda" with a kasra on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba', which is the reading of Mujahid and Ibn Muhays, its singular being "lubda" with a damma on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on both the lam and the ba', which is the reading of Abu Haywa, its singular being "lubayd"; and "lubbad" with a damma on the lam and a shadda on the ba', which is the reading of al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far, its singular being "labid," like "raki'" (kneeling) from "raka'a" and "sajid" from "sajada."

﴿قالَ﴾ meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is with this reading that most of the readers recited. Abu Ja'far, al-A'mash, 'Asim and Hamza read ﴿قُلْ﴾ as an imperative: ﴿إِنَّما أَدْعُوا رَبِّي وَلا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ أَحَدٌ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً﴾ meaning a refuge to which I may incline. Qatada said: "Support." Al-Kalbi: "An entrance into the earth like a tunnel." Al-Suddi: "A refuge."

Muqatil said: The Quraysh disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You have come with a great matter the like of which has never been heard, and you have opposed all the people. So return from this matter, and we will reward you." So Allah revealed these verses.

In the reading of Ubayy: "'anna wa la rashadan" (instead of "lakum darran wa la rashadan").

﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِسالاتِهِ﴾ for in it is the return, the security and the deliverance, said al-Hasan.

Qatada said: ﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ — that is what I possess, by the help and success of Allah; as for disbelief and faith, I do not possess them.

It was said: ﴿لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً﴾ — but I convey a message from Allah; I am only a messenger and a conveyor, possessing nothing except what I have been given.

﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً﴾ ﴿حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا ما يُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment.

﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ ناصِراً وَأَقَلُّ عَدَداً﴾ ﴿قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment; it was also said: the Resurrection. ﴿أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أَمَداً﴾ a term whose duration is long, an extended end.

﴿عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ﴾ is in the nominative as an adjective of "my Lord" (rabbi). It was also said: it is "the Knower of the unseen." ﴿فَلا يُظْهِرُ﴾ He does not cause to know ﴿عَلى غَيْبِهِ أَحَداً﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضى﴾ chosen ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a messenger; for He chooses him and informs him of what He wills of the unseen.

﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ He mentions some directions as an indication of all of them, ﴿رَصَداً﴾ guardians from among the angels who protect him from the devils and from the jinn's eavesdropping, lest they steal something and convey it to their soothsayers.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: ﴿رَصَداً﴾ are four guardian angels. Muqatil and others said: When Allah sent a messenger, Iblis would come to him in the form of Jibril to inform him. So Allah sent, ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً﴾ angels to guard him and drive away the devil. When a devil came to him in the form of an angel, they would say: "This is a devil, so beware." And when an angel came to him, they would say: "This is the messenger of your Lord."

﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ya', meaning: that people may know that the messengers have conveyed. The others read it with a fatha on the ya', meaning: that the Messenger may know that the angels ﴿أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ have conveyed the messages of their Lord. ﴿وَأَحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ — with what is with them, ﴿وَأَحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَداً﴾ so that nothing was hidden from him. "'Adadan" is in the accusative as a circumstantial (ḥāl); and if you wish, as a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning he counted a counting.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 72, verse 16–28:

﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا﴾ The reading of the common readers (al-'amma) is "law" with a kasra on the waw. Al-A'mash read "lawu" with a damma on the waw.

﴿عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ The exegetes differed in its interpretation. A group said: its meaning is, "And that if they had remained upon the way of truth, faith and guidance, and had been believers and obedient," ﴿لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ ماءً غَدَقاً﴾. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding this verse: "Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is trial (fitna)." He meant: We would have given them much wealth, a comfortable life, widened their provision and spread out for them in this world, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ that We might test them, to see how they would thank Him for what they were granted. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, Qatada, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Atiyya, Muqatil and al-Hasan. He said: "By Allah, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were listening to Allah and obeying Him when the treasures of Kisra and Caesar were opened to them, and they were tested by them, so they rose against their Imam and killed him, meaning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 66.] And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 96.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَياةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 97.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً﴾ [Surah Nuh: 10–11.] and other verses.

Others said: its meaning is, ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى طريقة الكفر والضلالة﴾ "And that if they had remained upon the way of disbelief and misguidance, and had all been disbelievers, We would have given them much wealth and widened for them, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ as a punishment for them and a gradual leading (istidraj), until they would be tested and We would punish them."

This is the view of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Kalbi, al-Thumali, Yaman ibn Rabab, Ibn Kaysan and Ibn Mujallad. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 44.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 33.]

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 27.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ [Surah al-'Alaq: 6–7.]

﴿وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ﴾ The readers of Kufa, Ya'qub and Ayyub read it with the letter ya (yaslukhu, "He will cause him to enter"), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd. Muslim ibn Jundab read "nuslikhu" with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the lam. The others read it with a fatha on the nun and a damma on the lam. Both are dialectal forms: "salaka" and "aslaka" have the same meaning, namely "to cause to enter."

﴿عَذاباً صَعَداً﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Arduous." Al-Suddi: "Hardship." Qatada: "There is no relief in it." Muqatil: "There is no release in it." Al-Hasan: "It only increases in severity."

Ibn Zayd: "Exhausting." The root meaning of this is that ascending (su'ud) is difficult for a person, and from it is 'Umar's saying: "Nothing has made me climb (tasa'uduni) as much as a marriage proposal," meaning it was difficult for me. 'Ikrima said: it is a mountain in the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira will be commanded to ascend in the Fire a mountain of smooth rock, until he reaches its summit, being pulled from in front with chains and struck with iron maces, until he reaches its top, yet he will not reach it for forty years. When he reaches its top, he will be dragged down to its base, and then he will again be commanded to ascend it. That is his condition forever. This is His saying: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾ [Surah al-Muddaththir: 17.]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The jinn said to the Prophet of Allah: "How can we come to the mosque and witness the prayer with you, when we are far from you?" So this was revealed: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾.

It was also said: it is "the Knower of the unseen." ﴿فَلا يُظْهِرُ﴾ He does not cause to know ﴿عَلى غَيْبِهِ أَحَداً﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضى﴾ chosen ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a messenger; for He chooses him and informs him of what He wills of the unseen.

﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ He mentions some directions as an indication of all of them, ﴿رَصَداً﴾ guardians from among the angels who protect him from the devils and from the jinn's eavesdropping, lest they steal something and convey it to their soothsayers.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: ﴿رَصَداً﴾ are four guardian angels. Muqatil and others said: When Allah sent a messenger, Iblis would come to him in the form of Jibril to inform him. So Allah sent, ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً﴾ angels to guard him and drive away the devil. When a devil came to him in the form of an angel, they would say: "This is a devil, so beware." And when an angel came to him, they would say: "This is the messenger of your Lord."

﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ya', meaning: that people may know that the messengers have conveyed. The others read it with a fatha on the ya', meaning: that the Messenger may know that the angels ﴿أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ have conveyed the messages of their Lord. ﴿وَأَحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ — with what is with them, ﴿وَأَحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَداً﴾ so that nothing was hidden from him. "'Adadan" is in the accusative as a circumstantial (ḥāl); and if you wish, as a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning he counted a counting.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 72, verse 16–28:

﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا﴾ The reading of the common readers (al-'amma) is "law" with a kasra on the waw. Al-A'mash read "lawu" with a damma on the waw.

﴿عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ The exegetes differed in its interpretation. A group said: its meaning is, "And that if they had remained upon the way of truth, faith and guidance, and had been believers and obedient," ﴿لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ ماءً غَدَقاً﴾. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding this verse: "Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is trial (fitna)." He meant: We would have given them much wealth, a comfortable life, widened their provision and spread out for them in this world, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ that We might test them, to see how they would thank Him for what they were granted. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, Qatada, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Atiyya, Muqatil and al-Hasan. He said: "By Allah, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were listening to Allah and obeying Him when the treasures of Kisra and Caesar were opened to them, and they were tested by them, so they rose against their Imam and killed him, meaning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 66.] And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 96.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَياةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 97.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً﴾ [Surah Nuh: 10–11.] and other verses.

Others said: its meaning is, ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى طريقة الكفر والضلالة﴾ "And that if they had remained upon the way of disbelief and misguidance, and had all been disbelievers, We would have given them much wealth and widened for them, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ as a punishment for them and a gradual leading (istidraj), until they would be tested and We would punish them."

This is the view of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Kalbi, al-Thumali, Yaman ibn Rabab, Ibn Kaysan and Ibn Mujallad. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 44.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 33.]

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 27.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ [Surah al-'Alaq: 6–7.]

﴿وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ﴾ The readers of Kufa, Ya'qub and Ayyub read it with the letter ya (yaslukhu, "He will cause him to enter"), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd. Muslim ibn Jundab read "nuslikhu" with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the lam. The others read it with a fatha on the nun and a damma on the lam. Both are dialectal forms: "salaka" and "aslaka" have the same meaning, namely "to cause to enter."

﴿عَذاباً صَعَداً﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Arduous." Al-Suddi: "Hardship." Qatada: "There is no relief in it." Muqatil: "There is no release in it." Al-Hasan: "It only increases in severity."

Ibn Zayd: "Exhausting." The root meaning of this is that ascending (su'ud) is difficult for a person, and from it is 'Umar's saying: "Nothing has made me climb (tasa'uduni) as much as a marriage proposal," meaning it was difficult for me. 'Ikrima said: it is a mountain in the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira will be commanded to ascend in the Fire a mountain of smooth rock, until he reaches its summit, being pulled from in front with chains and struck with iron maces, until he reaches its top, yet he will not reach it for forty years. When he reaches its top, he will be dragged down to its base, and then he will again be commanded to ascend it. That is his condition forever. This is His saying: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾ [Surah al-Muddaththir: 17.]

﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The jinn said to the Prophet of Allah: "How can we come to the mosque and witness the prayer with you, when we are far from you?" So this was revealed: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾.

Qatada said: When the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated partners with Allah, so Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers to make their supplication purely for Him when they entered the mosques, and He meant by it all the mosques.

Al-Hasan said: He meant by it all the lands, because the earth was made a mosque for the Prophet (ﷺ), and after the revelation of this verse, when one of the Muslims entered a mosque he would say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Talq ibn Habib said: By "mosques" is meant the limbs upon which the servant prostrates, and they are seven: the two feet, the two knees, the two hands and the face. I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sulami say:

I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qayyim al-Bazzaz say: Ibn 'Ata' said: "Your mosques are your limbs upon which you were commanded to prostrate; do not abase them to other than their Creator."

And Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya informed us more than once, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Hamdan al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il, Mu'alla ibn Asad and Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, they said: Wuhayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Tawus narrated to us from his father from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to prostrate upon seven: the bridge of the nose (indicating his nose with his hand), the forehead, the two hands, the two knees and the tips of the two feet, and that I should not gather up hair or clothing." [39] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/292.]

And Abu Bakr al-Juzuqi informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Basri informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to us from Ibn al-Had from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from 'Amir ibn Sa'd from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the servant prostrates, seven prostrate with him." [40] [Kitab al-Musnad li al-Shafi'i: 40.]

If "mosques" is taken to mean places, its singular is "masjid" with a kasra on the jim; if it is taken to mean the limbs, its singular is "masjid" with a fatha on the jim.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾ means the prayers. ﴿فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾ means: single Him out with tawhid and devote worship to Him sincerely. It was said: its meaning is, devote them to the remembrance of Allah and His worship, so do not make them a marketplace, a meeting place or a thoroughfare, and do not allot to other than Allah any share in them.

﴿وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ﴾ meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿يَدْعُوهُ﴾ saying: "There is no god but Allah," and calling to Him and reciting the Qur'an, ﴿كادُوا﴾ meaning the jinn, ﴿يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً﴾ meaning they would ride upon one another, crowd and fall over one another, out of eagerness to listen to the Qur'an. This was said by al-Dahhak, and 'Ata' related it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from him: This is the words of a group of the jinn when they returned to their people and informed them of what they had seen of the obedience of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to him, and their concern for him in bowing and prostration, and their following him in prayer.

Al-Hasan, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: It means that when 'Abd Allah stood with the call, the jinn and the humans gathered together and backed one another against him, to nullify the truth he had brought and to extinguish the light of Allah. But Allah refused except to complete this matter, support it and make it prevail over those who opposed it.

The root of "lubad" is groups piled upon one another; from it the large locust is called "labad," and hair is said to be "tallabbada" when it accumulates. From it the mane (lubda) of a lion takes its name, and its plural is "lubad." Zuhayr said:

*Before a lion, armed with weapons, fierce, having a mane whose claws have not been trimmed.* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/24.]

It has four readings: "lubad" with a kasra on the lam and a fatha on the ba' — and this is the reading of the common readers and the choice of Abu 'Ubayda and Abu Hatim, its singular being "lubda" with a kasra on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba', which is the reading of Mujahid and Ibn Muhays, its singular being "lubda" with a damma on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on both the lam and the ba', which is the reading of Abu Haywa, its singular being "lubayd"; and "lubbad" with a damma on the lam and a shadda on the ba', which is the reading of al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far, its singular being "labid," like "raki'" (kneeling) from "raka'a" and "sajid" from "sajada."

﴿قالَ﴾ meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is with this reading that most of the readers recited. Abu Ja'far, al-A'mash, 'Asim and Hamza read ﴿قُلْ﴾ as an imperative: ﴿إِنَّما أَدْعُوا رَبِّي وَلا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ أَحَدٌ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً﴾ meaning a refuge to which I may incline. Qatada said: "Support." Al-Kalbi: "An entrance into the earth like a tunnel." Al-Suddi: "A refuge."

Muqatil said: The Quraysh disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You have come with a great matter the like of which has never been heard, and you have opposed all the people. So return from this matter, and we will reward you." So Allah revealed these verses.

In the reading of Ubayy: "'anna wa la rashadan" (instead of "lakum darran wa la rashadan").

﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِسالاتِهِ﴾ for in it is the return, the security and the deliverance, said al-Hasan.

Qatada said: ﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ — that is what I possess, by the help and success of Allah; as for disbelief and faith, I do not possess them.

It was said: ﴿لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً﴾ — but I convey a message from Allah; I am only a messenger and a conveyor, possessing nothing except what I have been given.

﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً﴾ ﴿حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا ما يُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment.

﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ ناصِراً وَأَقَلُّ عَدَداً﴾ ﴿قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment; it was also said: the Resurrection. ﴿أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أَمَداً﴾ a term whose duration is long, an extended end.

It was also said: it is "the Knower of the unseen." ﴿فَلا يُظْهِرُ﴾ He does not cause to know ﴿عَلى غَيْبِهِ أَحَداً﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضى﴾ chosen ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a messenger; for He chooses him and informs him of what He wills of the unseen.

﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ He mentions some directions as an indication of all of them, ﴿رَصَداً﴾ guardians from among the angels who protect him from the devils and from the jinn's eavesdropping, lest they steal something and convey it to their soothsayers.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: ﴿رَصَداً﴾ are four guardian angels. Muqatil and others said: When Allah sent a messenger, Iblis would come to him in the form of Jibril to inform him. So Allah sent, ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً﴾ angels to guard him and drive away the devil. When a devil came to him in the form of an angel, they would say: "This is a devil, so beware." And when an angel came to him, they would say: "This is the messenger of your Lord."

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 27.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ [Surah al-'Alaq: 6–7.]

﴿وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ﴾ The readers of Kufa, Ya'qub and Ayyub read it with the letter ya (yaslukhu, "He will cause him to enter"), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd. Muslim ibn Jundab read "nuslikhu" with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the lam. The others read it with a fatha on the nun and a damma on the lam. Both are dialectal forms: "salaka" and "aslaka" have the same meaning, namely "to cause to enter."

﴿عَذاباً صَعَداً﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Arduous." Al-Suddi: "Hardship." Qatada: "There is no relief in it." Muqatil: "There is no release in it." Al-Hasan: "It only increases in severity."

Ibn Zayd: "Exhausting." The root meaning of this is that ascending (su'ud) is difficult for a person, and from it is 'Umar's saying: "Nothing has made me climb (tasa'uduni) as much as a marriage proposal," meaning it was difficult for me. 'Ikrima said: it is a mountain in the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira will be commanded to ascend in the Fire a mountain of smooth rock, until he reaches its summit, being pulled from in front with chains and struck with iron maces, until he reaches its top, yet he will not reach it for forty years. When he reaches its top, he will be dragged down to its base, and then he will again be commanded to ascend it. That is his condition forever. This is His saying: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾ [Surah al-Muddaththir: 17.]

﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The jinn said to the Prophet of Allah: "How can we come to the mosque and witness the prayer with you, when we are far from you?" So this was revealed: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾.

Qatada said: When the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated partners with Allah, so Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers to make their supplication purely for Him when they entered the mosques, and He meant by it all the mosques.

Al-Hasan said: He meant by it all the lands, because the earth was made a mosque for the Prophet (ﷺ), and after the revelation of this verse, when one of the Muslims entered a mosque he would say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Talq ibn Habib said: By "mosques" is meant the limbs upon which the servant prostrates, and they are seven: the two feet, the two knees, the two hands and the face. I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sulami say:

I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qayyim al-Bazzaz say: Ibn 'Ata' said: "Your mosques are your limbs upon which you were commanded to prostrate; do not abase them to other than their Creator."

And Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya informed us more than once, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Hamdan al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il, Mu'alla ibn Asad and Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, they said: Wuhayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Tawus narrated to us from his father from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to prostrate upon seven: the bridge of the nose (indicating his nose with his hand), the forehead, the two hands, the two knees and the tips of the two feet, and that I should not gather up hair or clothing." [39] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/292.]

And Abu Bakr al-Juzuqi informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Basri informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to us from Ibn al-Had from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from 'Amir ibn Sa'd from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the servant prostrates, seven prostrate with him." [40] [Kitab al-Musnad li al-Shafi'i: 40.]

If "mosques" is taken to mean places, its singular is "masjid" with a kasra on the jim; if it is taken to mean the limbs, its singular is "masjid" with a fatha on the jim.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ﴾ means the prayers. ﴿فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً﴾ means: single Him out with tawhid and devote worship to Him sincerely. It was said: its meaning is, devote them to the remembrance of Allah and His worship, so do not make them a marketplace, a meeting place or a thoroughfare, and do not allot to other than Allah any share in them.

﴿وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ﴾ meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿يَدْعُوهُ﴾ saying: "There is no god but Allah," and calling to Him and reciting the Qur'an, ﴿كادُوا﴾ meaning the jinn, ﴿يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً﴾ meaning they would ride upon one another, crowd and fall over one another, out of eagerness to listen to the Qur'an. This was said by al-Dahhak, and 'Ata' related it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from him: This is the words of a group of the jinn when they returned to their people and informed them of what they had seen of the obedience of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to him, and their concern for him in bowing and prostration, and their following him in prayer.

Al-Hasan, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: It means that when 'Abd Allah stood with the call, the jinn and the humans gathered together and backed one another against him, to nullify the truth he had brought and to extinguish the light of Allah. But Allah refused except to complete this matter, support it and make it prevail over those who opposed it.

The root of "lubad" is groups piled upon one another; from it the large locust is called "labad," and hair is said to be "tallabbada" when it accumulates. From it the mane (lubda) of a lion takes its name, and its plural is "lubad." Zuhayr said:

*Before a lion, armed with weapons, fierce, having a mane whose claws have not been trimmed.* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/24.]

It has four readings: "lubad" with a kasra on the lam and a fatha on the ba' — and this is the reading of the common readers and the choice of Abu 'Ubayda and Abu Hatim, its singular being "lubda" with a kasra on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba', which is the reading of Mujahid and Ibn Muhays, its singular being "lubda" with a damma on the lam; "lubud" with a damma on both the lam and the ba', which is the reading of Abu Haywa, its singular being "lubayd"; and "lubbad" with a damma on the lam and a shadda on the ba', which is the reading of al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far, its singular being "labid," like "raki'" (kneeling) from "raka'a" and "sajid" from "sajada."

﴿قالَ﴾ meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is with this reading that most of the readers recited. Abu Ja'far, al-A'mash, 'Asim and Hamza read ﴿قُلْ﴾ as an imperative: ﴿إِنَّما أَدْعُوا رَبِّي وَلا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً، قُلْ إِنِّي لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ أَحَدٌ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً﴾ meaning a refuge to which I may incline. Qatada said: "Support." Al-Kalbi: "An entrance into the earth like a tunnel." Al-Suddi: "A refuge."

Muqatil said: The Quraysh disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You have come with a great matter the like of which has never been heard, and you have opposed all the people. So return from this matter, and we will reward you." So Allah revealed these verses.

In the reading of Ubayy: "'anna wa la rashadan" (instead of "lakum darran wa la rashadan").

﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِسالاتِهِ﴾ for in it is the return, the security and the deliverance, said al-Hasan.

Qatada said: ﴿إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ — that is what I possess, by the help and success of Allah; as for disbelief and faith, I do not possess them.

It was said: ﴿لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً﴾ — but I convey a message from Allah; I am only a messenger and a conveyor, possessing nothing except what I have been given.

﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً﴾ ﴿حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا ما يُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment.

﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ ناصِراً وَأَقَلُّ عَدَداً﴾ ﴿قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ meaning the punishment; it was also said: the Resurrection. ﴿أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أَمَداً﴾ a term whose duration is long, an extended end.

﴿عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ﴾ is in the nominative as an adjective of "my Lord" (rabbi). It was also said: it is "the Knower of the unseen." ﴿فَلا يُظْهِرُ﴾ He does not cause to know ﴿عَلى غَيْبِهِ أَحَداً﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضى﴾ chosen ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a messenger; for He chooses him and informs him of what He wills of the unseen.

﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ He mentions some directions as an indication of all of them, ﴿رَصَداً﴾ guardians from among the angels who protect him from the devils and from the jinn's eavesdropping, lest they steal something and convey it to their soothsayers.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: ﴿رَصَداً﴾ are four guardian angels. Muqatil and others said: When Allah sent a messenger, Iblis would come to him in the form of Jibril to inform him. So Allah sent, ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً﴾ angels to guard him and drive away the devil. When a devil came to him in the form of an angel, they would say: "This is a devil, so beware." And when an angel came to him, they would say: "This is the messenger of your Lord."

﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ya', meaning: that people may know that the messengers have conveyed. The others read it with a fatha on the ya', meaning: that the Messenger may know that the angels ﴿أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ have conveyed the messages of their Lord. ﴿وَأَحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ — with what is with them, ﴿وَأَحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَداً﴾ so that nothing was hidden from him. "'Adadan" is in the accusative as a circumstantial (ḥāl); and if you wish, as a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning he counted a counting.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 72, verse 16–28:

﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا﴾ The reading of the common readers (al-'amma) is "law" with a kasra on the waw. Al-A'mash read "lawu" with a damma on the waw.

﴿عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ The exegetes differed in its interpretation. A group said: its meaning is, "And that if they had remained upon the way of truth, faith and guidance, and had been believers and obedient," ﴿لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ ماءً غَدَقاً﴾. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding this verse: "Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is trial (fitna)." He meant: We would have given them much wealth, a comfortable life, widened their provision and spread out for them in this world, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ that We might test them, to see how they would thank Him for what they were granted. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, Qatada, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Atiyya, Muqatil and al-Hasan. He said: "By Allah, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were listening to Allah and obeying Him when the treasures of Kisra and Caesar were opened to them, and they were tested by them, so they rose against their Imam and killed him, meaning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 66.] And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكاتٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 96.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَياةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 97.] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً﴾ [Surah Nuh: 10–11.] and other verses.

Others said: its meaning is, ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى طريقة الكفر والضلالة﴾ "And that if they had remained upon the way of disbelief and misguidance, and had all been disbelievers, We would have given them much wealth and widened for them, ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ as a punishment for them and a gradual leading (istidraj), until they would be tested and We would punish them."

This is the view of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Kalbi, al-Thumali, Yaman ibn Rabab, Ibn Kaysan and Ibn Mujallad. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 44.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 33.]

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 27.]

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ [Surah al-'Alaq: 6–7.]
